purpose: Profile-free content and logical-connection base for the iterated CLI-authored development review boards.

cards.body: Chicken evolution • tree, network & human history

**Scope**

A complete decision-useful backbone from cellular life to domestic chicken—not every named stem clade or population. Nested clades form the spine; fossils sit on side branches; domestication adds gene-flow and cultural networks.

**Executive synthesis**

Chicken is a living theropod dinosaur, nested within crown birds → Galloanserae → Galliformes → Phasianidae → Gallini → *Gallus*. Domestic ancestry is principally red-junglefowl/*spadiceus*-related, then reticulated by regional and cross-species gene flow.

**Evidence legend**

HIGH = replicated or convergent support. MODERATE = model/context sensitive. CONTESTED = live alternatives. Dates are tagged **fossil minimum**, **model estimate**, or **archaeological appearance**.

**AI boundary**

No Eido AI was run. The six Ask AI Cards below are deliberately unrun research questions. If run later, configure exactly `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` through OpenRouter first.
1 — Ancestral clade spine and fossil side branches

**Root scaffold → Archosauria**

Cellular organisms → Eukaryota → Opisthokonta → Metazoa → Bilateria → Deuterostomia → Chordata → Vertebrata → Gnathostomata → Osteichthyes/Euteleostomi → Sarcopterygii → Tetrapoda → Amniota → Sauropsida → Diapsida → Sauria → Archelosauria → Archosauria.

Nomenclatural scaffold: [NCBI Taxonomy](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=9031).

**Bird-line archosaurs**

Archosauria split into crocodile-line and bird-line branches. *Teleocrater* shows a diverse bird-line by about 245 Ma. **HIGH nesting; date is fossil occurrence.** [Nesbitt 2017](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature22037)

**Dinosauria**

Early well-sampled dinosaur assemblages occur by roughly 230 Ma; exact early branching remains revisable. **MODERATE–HIGH appearance window.** [Sereno 2011](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1198467)

**Theropod lineage**

The chicken lineage runs through saurischian theropods in the topology used here. Birds never stopped being dinosaurs. **HIGH broad nesting.** [Brusatte 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2014.08.034)

**Tetanurae → Coelurosauria**

Bird-like anatomy accumulated piecemeal across many theropod branches rather than in one leap. **HIGH broad pattern.** [Brusatte 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2014.08.034)

**Maniraptora → Paraves**

Sustained miniaturization preceded birds for about 50 Myr across roughly 12 branches. **HIGH trend; model-dependent rate.** [Lee 2014](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1252243)

**Avialae**

Late Jurassic avialans document early bird-grade flight experiments; local paravian placement remains dataset-sensitive. **HIGH occurrence; CONTESTED local topology.** [Pei 2020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2020.06.105)

**Pygostylia / short-tailed avialans**

Tail shortening, vertebral reduction, and terminal fusion evolved stepwise. New Jurassic fossils sharpen—but do not settle—the earliest pygostylian node.

**Ornithothoraces**

The major Cretaceous radiation includes extinct Enantiornithes and the euornithine line toward crown birds. This is a nested clade path, not a list of direct ancestors.

**Ornithuromorpha**

A crownward avialan grouping on the line toward living birds. It is not interchangeable with every use of Euornithes; definitions and fossil membership vary among matrices.

**Euornithes, as defined in the selected matrix**

A crownward waypoint before Aves. Fossils constrain minimum ages; fragmentary specimens and clade definitions can change local placement.

**Aves / Neornithes (crown birds)**

Genome-scale studies recover Palaeognathae + Neognathae; rapid early divergences retain gene-tree conflict. **HIGH topology; exact dates actively disputed by clock/calibration choices.** [Stiller 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07323-1); [Wu 2024](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2319696121); [Claramunt critique](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2405887121)

**Neognathae**

The living backbone splits into Galloanserae and Neoaves. Short internodes and incomplete lineage sorting explain residual genomic discordance. [Jarvis 2014](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1253451)

**Galloanserae**

Landfowl + waterfowl share a deep crown-bird ancestor. *Asteriornis* documents the broader total group before K–Pg; *Conflicto* supplies the safest 65.65 Ma minimum for the internal landfowl–waterfowl crown split.

**Galliformes (landfowl)**

Five-family backbone: Megapodiidae + (Cracidae + (Numididae + (Odontophoridae + Phasianidae))). **HIGH topology; MODERATE dates.** [Chen 2021](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-021-01935-1)

**Phasianidae**

The pheasant family contains the chicken lineage. Family-scale UCE sampling resolves broad placement more safely than exact divergence times. [Kimball 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ympev.2021.107091)

**Phasianinae → Gallini**

Bamboo partridges (*Bambusicola*) are the nearest sampled living genus to *Gallus* in genome/UCE analyses. **MODERATE–HIGH.** [Tiley 2020](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40657-020-00194-w)

**Gallus**

Four living wild species: red, green, grey, and Sri Lanka junglefowl. Grey + Sri Lanka is stable; whether red or green is deepest remains contested.

**Domestic chicken**

Nested within red-junglefowl diversity, with a principal *G. g. spadiceus*-related surviving source plus later gene flow. **HIGH principal ancestry; origin settlement unresolved.** [Wang 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41422-020-0349-y)

**Method rule: fossil ≠ ancestor**

The named fossils below illuminate or calibrate branches. None is demonstrated to be the chicken's direct ancestor; stem, crown, and total-group placements are kept distinct.

**Crocodile-line archosaurs**

Living crocodilians occupy the other major archosaur branch. They are evolutionary cousins, not steps on the chicken spine.

† **Teleocrater — ~245 Ma**

A bird-line side relative revealing early character mosaics. **FOSSIL OCCURRENCE; not ancestor.** [Nesbitt 2017](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature22037)

† **Archaeopteryx mosaic — ~150 Ma**

The Chicago specimen combines primitive dinosaurian anatomy with flight-related plumage and structures. Occurrence is secure but exact paravian placement remains analysis-sensitive. **Not a demonstrated chicken ancestor.** [O'Connor 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08912-4); [Rauhut 2018](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.4191)

† **Baminornis — Jurassic tail debate**

Proposed as the earliest short-tailed/pygostylian bird, but the fused series' interpretation is disputed. **CONTESTED morphology.** [2025 description](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08410-z); [2026 critique](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cretres.2025.106244)

† **Zhengheornis — stepwise tail evolution**

Tail shortening and vertebral reduction preceded terminal fusion, supporting mosaic evolution rather than a single pygostyle leap. [Wang 2026](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aeb5202)

† **Enantiornithes — extinct ornithothoracines**

A diverse Cretaceous sister radiation outside the euornithine line to living birds. Their success and extinction show that avialan history was a branching bush, not a ladder.

**K–Pg survival filter — 66 Ma**

Forest collapse may have favored non-arboreal crown-bird lineages. **Tested ecological inference, not direct observation.** [Field 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2018.04.062)

**Palaeognathae**

The sister branch to Neognathae within living crown birds. Included to show the full crown split, not as a chicken ancestor.

**Neoaves**

The sister branch to Galloanserae within Neognathae. Most living bird diversity lies here, outside the chicken path.

† **Asteriornis — 66.8–66.7 Ma**

Best-supported latest-Cretaceous crown bird near total Galloanserae. Its stem-galliform versus broader stem-galloanseran placement varies. **HIGH occurrence; not a modern chicken.** [Field 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2096-0)

**Anseriformes (waterfowl)**

The living sister order to Galliformes within Galloanserae.

† **Vegavis — 69.2–68.4 Ma**

A new skull supports crown-waterfowl placement, but a 2026 mandibular analysis found no unambiguous anseriform characters and only weak recovery. **CONTESTED conditional fossil constraint—not ‘oldest duck’.** [Torres 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08390-0); [Crane 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-025-02487-4)

† **Conflicto — 66.04–65.65 Ma**

Secure total-group waterfowl. Its youngest bound gives the safest current **65.65 Ma minimum for crown Galloanserae**. [Tambussi 2019](https://doi.org/10.1093/zoolinnean/zly085)

† **Gallinuloides — 51.6 Ma**

A Paleogene stem galliform basal to living landfowl. It fills part of the fossil gap but does **not** date crown Phasianidae. [Ksepka 2009](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1096-0031.2009.00250.x)
2 — Galliform family tree and the unresolved Gallus fork

**Galliform crown root**

Model estimate near 71.7 Ma in one UCE clock; topology is safer than the exact number. [Chen 2021](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-021-01935-1)

**Megapodiidae**

Basal living family in the recovered five-family Galliform topology.

**Remaining landfowl after Megapodiidae**

A structural branch point; date estimates remain calibration-sensitive.

**Cracidae**

Next family branch; one model estimates the split near 62.4 Ma. **MODEL ESTIMATE.** [Chen 2021](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-021-01935-1)

**Remaining landfowl after Cracidae**

Leads to Numididae and the Odontophoridae–Phasianidae pair.

**Numididae**

Guineafowl branch; one model estimates the split near 41.3 Ma. **MODEL ESTIMATE.** [Chen 2021](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-021-01935-1)

**Final family sister pair**

Odontophoridae + Phasianidae; their split is estimated near 39.9 Ma in one analysis. **MODEL ESTIMATE.** [Chen 2021](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-021-01935-1)

**Odontophoridae**

New World quail family; sister to Phasianidae in the family-complete topology.

**Phasianidae focus**

Crown family estimated near 35.4 Ma in one model. Dense UCE sampling supports topology; heterogeneous missing data cautions against overreading rates. [Kimball 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ympev.2021.107091)

**Gallini focus**

The tribe containing *Gallus* and *Bambusicola*.

**Bambusicola**

Nearest sampled living genus to *Gallus*; split near 15–16 Ma is a **MODEL ESTIMATE**. [Tiley 2020](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40657-020-00194-w)

**Gallus focus**

Living species radiation is reticulate: incomplete lineage sorting and introgression make a single bifurcating tree an approximation.

**Clock comparison — topology is safer than dates**

Crown Aves: 93.0 Ma (85.8–100.9) in Stiller and ~100 Ma (90.3–110.5) in a morphology/FBD analysis. Crown Galloanserae: 68.19 Ma (66.10–70.67) in Stiller versus 82.1 Ma (69.5–96.5) in Chen. **MODEL ESTIMATES, not observed appearances.** [Stiller 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07323-1); [Brocklehurst & Field 2024](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2023.2618); [Chen 2021](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-021-01935-1)

**Candidate topology A — green basal**

`Green,(Red,(Grey,Sri Lanka))`

Supported by Lawal/Tiley partitions. [Lawal 2020](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-020-0738-1)

**Candidate topology B — red basal**

`Red,(Green,(Grey,Sri Lanka))`

Favored by a multi-individual, contamination-screened SNP analysis. [Mariadassou 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ympev.2020.107044)

**Why both can look strong**

Introgression + incomplete lineage sorting produce different gene trees. High bootstrap support on concatenated data need not equal the species history. **CONTESTED.**

**Stable result**

Grey + Sri Lanka junglefowl form a sister pair across competing genome-scale analyses. **HIGH.**

**G. gallus — red junglefowl**

Five commonly recognized subspecies; domestic chicken is nested within its diversity.

**G. varius — green junglefowl**

Either deepest living *Gallus* branch or second branch, depending on the model.

**G. sonneratii — grey junglefowl**

Sister to Sri Lanka junglefowl. Multiple domestic regions show grey-related allele sharing, but broad direction, timing, and phenotype remain unresolved. The grey-derived **BCO2** haplotype is the validated donor-to-phenotype case.

**G. lafayettii — Sri Lanka junglefowl**

Sister to grey junglefowl; fewer geographically restricted candidate domestic introgression tracts.

**Domestic lineage within red junglefowl**

Primary surviving affinity is *spadiceus*-related. Domestic nomenclature varies; ancestry is clearer than rank.
3 — Domestication is a reticulate genomic network

**Principal surviving source**

A *G. g. spadiceus*-related population contributed most ancestry to sampled domestic chickens. **HIGH for surviving sampled lineages.** [Wang 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41422-020-0349-y)

**9,500 ± 3,300 years is not domestication**

It is a modeled domestic–*spadiceus* population split (12,800–6,200 years ago), not the start of human management. [Wang 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41422-020-0349-y)

**Domestic chicken ancestry hub**

A principal red-junglefowl lineage plus later regional red-junglefowl and cross-species inputs. The history is a network, not a clean single-origin tree.

**Regional red-junglefowl inputs**

*murghi* → sampled South Asian chickens; *bankiva* + *gallus* → sampled Indonesian chickens; *jabouillei* → some sampled Chinese chickens. Population estimates are not universal species fractions.

**Regional domestic mosaics**

Secondary ancestry accumulated after the principal lineage spread, preserving local contact histories.

**Grey ↔ domestic allele sharing / introgression**

Multiple tracts are the strongest non-red relationship, but broad direction and timing are not fixed by D/f4 statistics. Only cases such as **BCO2** justify a simple donor-to-phenotype arrow. [Lawal 2020](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-020-0738-1)

**BCO2 / yellow skin**

A grey-junglefowl-derived cis-regulatory haplotype causes yellow skin in many domestic chickens. **HIGH locus-level hybrid legacy.** [Eriksson 2008](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1000010)

**Sri Lanka → domestic candidates**

Fewer, geographically restricted candidate tracts. **MODERATE locus-level evidence.**

**Green → domestic candidate**

Rare compelling candidate tract(s), not a general origin contribution. **MODERATE.**

**Domestic → nominally wild backcrossing**

Gene flow also runs backward into living red-junglefowl populations.

**Modern ‘wild’ is porous**

Modern red junglefowl often carry more domestic ancestry than historical museum birds. Exact fractions are sample-sensitive. [Wu 2023](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.1010551)

**Grain-commensal pathway**

Cultivation may have concentrated food and repeated junglefowl–human contact. **Plausible MODERATE hypothesis, not a proven event.** [Peters 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2121978119)

**Archaeology supplies a minimum**

The earliest accepted assemblage is not necessarily the first management population. Secure occurrence, genetic divergence, domestic status, and economic exploitation are different milestones.

**Ban Non Wat, Thailand — ~1650–1250 BCE**

Earliest accepted **phase-associated chicken assemblage** in the conservative synthesis. Abundance, juveniles, village association, and rice agriculture support management, but domestic status remains contextual/inferential and the bones are not directly dated. **MODERATE contextual inference.** [Peters 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2121978119)
4 — Selected conservative dispersal and use anchors

**Route-map rule**

Dates below are secure appearances, not origin dates. Bone movement, intrusive contexts, uneven sampling, and cultural treatment complicate arrows between regions.

**Central/eastern China — ~1350–1046 BCE**

Secure late Shang evidence; early-Holocene northern claims are excluded from the main timeline. **MODERATE.** [Peters 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2121978119)

**South Asia — ~1500–1200 BCE**

Supported post-Harappan/early Jorwe appearances; classic early Indus-origin stories lack secure evidence in the conservative review. [Peters 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2121978119)

**Mesopotamia — late 2nd millennium/Iron Age I**

Appearances precede stronger economic use later in the first millennium BCE. **MODERATE.** [Peters 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2121978119)

**Ethiopia / Horn — ~800–600 BCE**

Directly dated occurrence is consistent with a Red Sea route; the route remains inferential. **MODERATE–HIGH occurrence.** [Peters 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2121978119)

**Mediterranean Europe — 8th/7th c. BCE**

Direct AMS dates moved many alleged early bones younger. **HIGH revised chronology.** [Best 2022](https://doi.org/10.15184/aqy.2021.90)

**Arrival ≠ routine food animal**

In parts of Europe, complete, old, or unbutchered birds suggest special treatment preceded routine consumption by centuries. **MODERATE contextual inference.** [Best 2022](https://doi.org/10.15184/aqy.2021.90)

**Near/Remote Oceania**

Direct bones place chickens in parts of the Solomons, Vanuatu, and Tonga by the early first millennium BCE; Hawai‘i is much later, around 1200 CE. **MODERATE; island chronologies vary.** [Peters 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2121978119)

**Madagascar / Comoros — ~750–900 CE**

Secure appearances; African maritime and overland contributions remain incompletely resolved. **MODERATE.** [Peters 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2121978119)

**Central Asia — 515–206 BCE onward**

Direct eggshell AMS plus separate microscopy/proteomics at multiple sites support regular consumption; density is compatible with regular egg supply, not proof of year-round prolific laying. [Peters 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46093-2)

**REJECTED MAIN-TIMELINE CLAIM: northern China ~10,000 BP**

Initial mtDNA claim failed later morphology/authentication tests; key remains were pheasants. [Xiang 2014](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1411882111); [Barton 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-59316-5)

**Karako-Kagi, Japan — 381–204 BCE**

Juvenile bones identified by ZooMS, with one directly dated femur. Compatible with local breeding at a major settlement; not the date chickens first entered East Asia. [Eda 2023](https://doi.org/10.3389/feart.2023.1104535)

**Maresha — late 4th–3rd c. BCE**

Two directly dated bones within a 1,092-remain, female-biased and butchered assemblage mark compelling large-scale economic exploitation in the southern Levant—not first arrival. [Perry-Gal 2015](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1504236112)

**UNAUDITABLE: Caiyuanzi, Yunnan — claimed ~2475–2205 BCE**

The alleged chicken was not figured or directly dated, so its identification cannot presently be evaluated and does not displace Ban Non Wat. [Peng 2022](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2210996119); [Peters reply](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2213678119)

**Gungok-ri, Korea — 80–361 CE**

Five *Gallus* bones were identified by ZooMS and directly dated; nitrogen isotopes support human feeding/management but do not independently prove domestication. [Kim 2026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jasrep.2025.105561)

**Finland / Baltic — 266–541 CE anchor**

The earliest directly dated Finnish specimen in a 2026 Baltic dataset adds regional dispersal and lineage history, not an origin or first-arrival date for Europe. [Olli 2026](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41437-026-00842-9)

**UNSUBSTANTIATED: El Arenal 1, Chile**

The original 1321–1407 CE specimen is unavailable for replication. Re-excavation found genuinely pre-/early-contact deposits, but reassessed and newly DNA-tested bird bones were tinamou. This is no secure archaeological chicken—not proof that all pre-contact transfer was impossible. [Bühring 2024](https://doi.org/10.1080/15564894.2023.2268551)
5 — Evidence lenses: what each can and cannot answer

**Comparative fossil anatomy**

Best for placing extinct side relatives and setting observed minimum ages. Failure modes: sparse preservation, convergence, and mistaking close relatives for ancestors.

**Stratigraphy + direct dating**

Best for establishing when a specimen existed. Failure modes: reworking, intrusive bones, and indirect layer dates.

**Genome-scale species trees**

Best for broad nesting and gene-tree discordance. Failure modes: concatenation hiding ILS and introgression turning trees into approximations.

**Molecular clocks / demographic models**

Estimate invisible divergence windows. Calibration, mutation rate, generation time, structure, and coalescent treatment matter; current crown-bird chronologies disagree, and population splits are not domestication events.

**Ancient DNA**

Tests identity and historical ancestry directly. Contamination, damage, tiny samples, and reference bias demand replication and authentication.

**Morphology / osteometry / ZooMS**

Broadens archaeological identification. Closely related galliform bones overlap; reference coverage and preservation constrain certainty.

**Archaeological context**

Shows association, treatment, diet, and movement. Presence at a settlement alone does not prove domestication.

**Modern population genomics**

Maps surviving ancestry and gene flow. Extinct sources are invisible; modern wild populations can be feral-introgressed and sampling is geographic.

**Triangulate, do not collapse**

Topology, fossil minima, demographic splits, archaeological appearances, and cultural use answer different questions. Agreement raises confidence; disagreement defines the research frontier.
6 — Open research program (Ask AI Cards are unrun)

**Open-question hub**

These prompts state discriminating evidence needs rather than invite unsupported completion. No model has answered them on this board.

**UNRUN — Where was the first management population?**

Design a directly dated ancient-genome sampling program across mainland Southeast Asia before and during 2000 BCE. Separate source-region affinity from settlement-level origin.

**UNRUN — What was pre-domestication red junglefowl genomically?**

Specify historical and archaeological reference panels across all five subspecies while controlling domestic backcrossing.

**UNRUN — Which Gallus topology survives explicit network models?**

Compare red-first and green-first trees using ILS + gene-flow models, ancient samples, and fossil-aware dating.

**UNRUN — Which introgressed tracts changed phenotype?**

Beyond **BCO2**, require genotype-to-phenotype validation before calling candidate tracts adaptive.

**UNRUN — Was egg production deliberately selected early?**

Combine seasonality, isotopes, medullary bone, husbandry context, and ancient genomes to distinguish abundance from selection.

**UNRUN — Did chickens reach South America before Europeans?**

Require replicated libraries, damage patterns, nuclear capture, isotopes, and additional directly dated bones.
